plans.title: Smart Expense Tracker — Full-Stack MVP
plans.purpose: Build and learn a polished AI-powered personal expense tracker end-to-end, from product foundations through frontend, FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL, authentication, AI insights, testing, and deployment.
learnings: With verbatimModuleSyntax enabled, React/TypeScript types such as FormEvent and ExpenseFormData must use `import type`; runtime values remain normal imports.
The current frontend step is intentionally local-state first: build interaction and validation before connecting FastAPI, so backend contracts are not invented prematurely.
Expense UI state is currently owned by Expenses.tsx; child components should communicate edits/deletes via typed callbacks rather than owning the list.
Use callback props from the Expenses page to keep the transaction collection as the single source of truth during the local-state phase.
Keep transaction collection state in Expenses.tsx and expose edit/delete through typed callbacks to child components.

For the database phase, keep PostgreSQL as the authoritative source of financial data, use NUMERIC for money, derive dashboard totals from transaction data rather than storing duplicate totals, and enforce user ownership through foreign keys plus backend authorization.
Added a human approval gate after database schema design so SQLAlchemy models and Alembic migrations cannot drift from an unapproved relational design.

The schema should support future AI analytics without storing AI-generated financial truth: FinancialInsight records can cache generated explanations/metadata, while all numeric financial facts remain derivable from core transaction, budget, and goal tables.
Database design phase is documentation-first: do not create ORM models or migrations until the schema is explicitly approved, because those artifacts become the implementation contract.

Use explicit ownership on core tables (user_id on categories, expenses, income, budgets, goals, insights) even where ownership could be inferred through another relation; this simplifies authorization queries and prevents accidental cross-user joins.
Keep Category user-owned with a uniqueness constraint on (user_id, name), allowing future custom categories without cross-user collisions.

steps.content: Finalize users, jobs-to-be-done, product principles, and MVP boundaries.
steps.implementation_outline: Confirm the individual personal-finance user, core use cases, must-have features, should-have features, and explicit out-of-scope items.
steps.verification: Review against the agreed product brief -> expected: one primary persona, actionable use cases, clear MVP boundaries -> PASS; must-fail: vague audience or unbounded scope.

steps.content: Finalize UX information architecture and visual direction before implementation.
steps.context: UX/information architecture is now the active implementation-planning step. Must complete and record outcome, then pause for user approval before starting the next step.
steps.human_approval_comments: User explicitly approved the completed UX/information architecture and requested to proceed to frontend.
steps.implementation_outline: Finalize the UX information architecture and wireframe-level specification: authenticated app shell, primary navigation, page hierarchy, dashboard layout, transaction flows, budget/goal flows, analytics and AI advisor entry points, responsive behavior, and calm premium visual direction. Keep all MVP capabilities discoverable without overloading the dashboard.
steps.verification: UX review -> page hierarchy, navigation, dashboard priorities, responsive behavior, and AI Advisor flow were explicitly presented to the user -> PASS. Must-fail check: user would reject/require changes if the hierarchy or core flows were not acceptable; user explicitly approved and requested to proceed -> PASS.
steps.outcome: Finalized the MVP UX/information architecture: public auth screens; authenticated Dashboard, Expenses, Income, Budgets, Savings Goals, Analytics, and AI Advisor; desktop sidebar, responsive mobile navigation, dashboard information hierarchy, transaction flows, budget/goal visuals, AI Advisor interaction, and calm premium Pinterest-inspired visual direction.

steps.content: Finalize full-stack architecture and development conventions.
steps.context: User asked when Step 3 can be started. It is now the active priority. We will finalize full-stack architecture and development conventions before proceeding further with backend/database/API implementation.
steps.implementation_outline: Lock frontend/backend boundaries, request flow, folder responsibilities, environment configuration, error handling, API versioning, naming conventions, and native fetch vs TanStack Query decision. Include Gemini as the AI provider behind a service abstraction and keep business logic out of React components and FastAPI routers.
steps.verification: Architecture review -> expected: clear React -> FastAPI router -> service -> repository/SQLAlchemy -> PostgreSQL flow, explicit external integration boundaries, environment/secrets policy, error and API versioning conventions, and no UI-embedded business logic -> PASS; must-fail: router-only monolith, business logic embedded in UI, undocumented provider boundary, or hard-coded secrets.
steps.outcome: Architecture finalized and documented in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/API_CONVENTIONS.md, and docs/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md. Stack, layer boundaries, API versioning, auth transport, money semantics, Gemini boundary, native fetch decision, and security/ownership rules are locked.

steps.content: Design PostgreSQL data model and relationships.
steps.context: The database design is now being written as a concrete schema contract in docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA.md; no SQLAlchemy/Alembic implementation is being performed in this step.
steps.implementation_outline: Create docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA.md containing the approved relational design for users, categories, expenses, income, budgets, savings goals, and financial insights, with explicit keys, constraints, indexes, ownership, delete behavior, money/date semantics, and derived-vs-persisted decisions.
steps.verification: Read docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA.md -> expected: complete normalized MVP schema with explicit relationships and integrity rules -> PASS. Must-fail: ambiguous ownership, missing foreign key, float money, or duplicate authoritative totals -> PASS; the document explicitly addresses ownership, foreign keys, NUMERIC money, indexes, delete behavior, and derived values.
steps.outcome: Completed the PostgreSQL relational design and saved it as docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA.md. The model covers users, user-owned categories, expenses, income, budgets, savings goals, and financial insight artifacts; defines relationships, ownership, constraints, indexes, deletion behavior, NUMERIC(12,2) money, DATE/TIMESTAMPTZ semantics, and calculated-vs-persisted data. SQLAlchemy/Alembic implementation has not started.

steps.content: Approve the database schema before SQLAlchemy implementation.
steps.context: The PostgreSQL schema is finalized in docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA.md. This approval gate must be explicitly approved before SQLAlchemy models, Alembic migrations, or database table creation begins.
steps.implementation_outline: Have the user review the schema design and explicitly approve it. Once approved, mark this gate approved and proceed to backend/ORM implementation.
steps.verification: User review -> expected: explicit approval to proceed -> PASS; must-fail: starting SQLAlchemy/Alembic implementation before approval.

steps.content: Create backend project skeleton and Python development environment.
steps.implementation_outline: Create backend app structure with core, models, schemas, routers, services, repositories, integrations, utils, tests, and Alembic; establish virtual environment and dependency management; add minimal FastAPI app.
steps.verification: Run FastAPI development server and health endpoint -> expected: HTTP 200 JSON response -> PASS; must-fail: app import/startup failure.

steps.content: Set up PostgreSQL locally and connect FastAPI through SQLAlchemy.
steps.implementation_outline: Create the application database, configure environment variables, create SQLAlchemy engine/session/base, connect safely, and verify a database connection through a controlled backend check.
steps.verification: Run database connectivity check -> expected: successful PostgreSQL connection and clean session lifecycle -> PASS; must-fail: hard-coded credentials or leaked secrets.

steps.content: Set up Alembic migrations and implement initial database models.
steps.implementation_outline: Create SQLAlchemy models from the approved schema, configure Alembic, generate the initial migration, apply it, and verify tables/constraints in PostgreSQL.
steps.verification: Run migration upgrade and inspect schema -> expected: all approved tables, foreign keys, indexes, and constraints exist -> PASS; must-fail: model/schema drift or migration failure.

steps.content: Define REST API contracts and shared frontend/backend data shapes.
steps.implementation_outline: Finalize /api/v1/auth, users, expenses, income, categories, budgets, goals, analytics, insights, and AI endpoints; define request/response schemas, status codes, validation errors, pagination/filter conventions.
steps.verification: Review OpenAPI docs and endpoint matrix -> expected: every MVP workflow maps to a documented endpoint and schema -> PASS; must-fail: undocumented client-critical endpoint or inconsistent response shape.

steps.content: Implement authentication and authorization foundation.
steps.implementation_outline: Implement registration/login/logout, secure password hashing, access/refresh token strategy with HttpOnly cookies, current-user dependency, protected routes, ownership checks, CORS, and security configuration.
steps.verification: Run auth tests -> expected: valid user authenticates, protected endpoint rejects unauthenticated request, User A cannot access User B data -> PASS; must-fail: plaintext passwords, token leakage, or missing ownership enforcement.

steps.content: Implement category, expense, and income CRUD APIs.
steps.implementation_outline: Build Pydantic schemas, routers, services, repositories where useful, validation, ownership enforcement, filtering, sorting, and pagination for financial transactions and categories.
steps.verification: Run API tests for create/read/update/delete and invalid inputs -> expected: correct persistence, validation, and user isolation -> PASS; must-fail: cross-user data access or inconsistent CRUD behavior.

steps.content: Implement dashboard analytics and core financial calculations.
steps.context: Paused intentionally so the plan returns to architecture before further feature work. The user asked when Step 3 can begin; Step 3 is now the priority because the architecture should be locked before backend/API/database implementation.
steps.implementation_outline: Resume after Step 3 architecture is finalized. Preserve the completed interactive Expenses work and continue dashboard financial exploration later without discarding it.
steps.verification: Step 3 architecture review must pass before returning to this step; no further feature implementation should depend on unfinalized backend boundaries.
steps.outcome: Paused after user-approved interactive Expenses pass so architecture can be finalized first.

steps.content: Build budgets and savings goals.
steps.implementation_outline: Implement budget creation/tracking, category or overall budget rules, progress calculations, savings-goal targets, contribution tracking, and goal progress summaries.
steps.verification: Run business-rule tests -> expected: progress and remaining amounts match fixture calculations and invalid states are rejected -> PASS; must-fail: negative/invalid financial states or incorrect ownership.

steps.content: Build the React application shell and routing.
steps.context: Tailwind/Vite styling foundation is implemented and the production build passes. Continue this step with React Router, application shell, sidebar/navigation, and page route scaffolding.
steps.implementation_outline: Create the visual shell, responsive sidebar/navigation, authenticated route structure, loading/error states, theme foundation, and pages for dashboard, expenses, income, budgets, goals, and AI advisor. Current sub-step: establish Tailwind/Vite styling foundation and replace the Vite starter screen; next sub-step after verification is React Router and application shell.
steps.verification: Run `npm run build` -> expected: TypeScript and Vite production build succeed -> PASS. Browser smoke check -> expected: dashboard renders with responsive sidebar/navigation and route scaffolding -> PASS. Must-fail: build errors or broken route rendering; user confirmed completion and supplied dashboard screenshot showing the application shell rendering.
steps.outcome: Built and verified the React application shell: Tailwind/Vite styling foundation, React Router integration, responsive AppLayout/sidebar/mobile navigation, dashboard and core route scaffolding, and reusable dashboard components. User confirmed the frontend shell is done and provided a rendered dashboard screenshot showing the sidebar, cards, spending overview, AI insight, budget pulse, and recent transactions.

steps.content: Implement the core frontend transaction and financial-management flows.
steps.context: Expense UX pass implemented after the approved Pinterest/editorial redesign. Added clickable transaction details with a responsive modal/drawer-style dialog, contextual Edit/Delete actions, corrected the insight copy so it matches the actual largest category, and kept local CRUD/search/filter behavior intact. Awaiting user build and interaction verification before marking this sub-step complete.
steps.implementation_outline: Continue the expense-flow UX pass: transaction detail interaction, accurate insight messaging, and accessibility-safe interaction targets. Then verify with production build and UI smoke tests before proceeding to income flows.
steps.verification: Run `npm run build` -> expected: TypeScript and Vite production build succeed -> PASS. UI smoke check -> expected: add-expense validation and local transaction creation work without runtime errors -> PASS. Next must-fail check: edit/delete must not mutate unrelated transactions or accept invalid edits.
steps.outcome: Implemented AddExpenseForm with controlled inputs, validation, category/date selection, and local transaction creation/search. Fixed type-only imports required by verbatimModuleSyntax; user confirmed the build passes. Next sub-step is edit/delete.

steps.content: Redesign the expense experience with a Pinterest-inspired, more interactive visual direction before implementation.
steps.context: User requested a better, more Pinteresty, interactive, appealing UI. This is a UX/mockup approval gate before changing project files.
steps.human_approval_comments: User approved the Pinterest-inspired interactive redesign direction and the AI/data architecture direction.
steps.implementation_outline: Define the expense-page visual system: editorial/card composition, warm neutral palette with a restrained accent, category imagery/visual cues, stronger hierarchy, interactive hover/focus states, quick-add interaction, filters/search treatment, transaction cards/list treatment, edit/delete affordances, empty states, and responsive behavior. Present the proposed direction for user review before implementation.
steps.verification: UX review -> expected: proposed visual direction and interaction model presented and explicitly approved -> PASS. Must-fail: implementation before approval -> not applicable; approval was received before implementation.
steps.outcome: User approved the redesign direction: Pinterest/editorial-inspired visual language, warmer and more visual composition, tactile transaction cards, interactive filters/quick-add, stronger AI insight presentation, and a product direction where deterministic financial analytics provide facts while Gemini handles natural-language understanding, contextual synthesis, pattern explanation, categorization, and conversational exploration.

steps.content: Complete expense edit/delete interactions and verify local transaction state behavior.
steps.context: User approved the interactive UX direction. Implement the approved interaction pass within the existing Expenses experience: clickable transaction details, category drill-down, contextual actions, quick-add, undo-friendly deletion, animated state transitions, and responsive mobile behavior. Keep data local until backend contracts exist.
steps.implementation_outline: Add reusable edit behavior to the existing expense UI, validate edited values, support deletion with a clear confirmation interaction, preserve unrelated transactions, and add lightweight undo/keyboard interaction polish without introducing API contracts.
steps.verification: Run `npm run build` -> expected: production build succeeds -> PASS. UI smoke check -> expected: edit changes only the selected expense, invalid edits are rejected, delete removes only the selected expense, undo restores the deleted expense, spending-mix/category actions filter correctly, and Escape closes detail view -> PASS; must-fail: duplicate IDs, cross-row mutation, runtime errors, or stale deletion state.
steps.outcome: Verified by the user: the interactive expense pass works. The expense page now supports local edit/delete interactions, transaction detail opening/closing, clickable spending-mix drill-down, an actionable pattern button, animated progress changes, delete undo feedback, and Escape-to-close behavior. No backend/API contracts were introduced.

steps.content: Build dashboard visualization and polished responsive UX.
steps.implementation_outline: Implement Recharts visualizations, summary cards, spending breakdowns, budget progress, goal progress, empty/loading/error states, responsive layouts, accessibility basics, and subtle motion only where it improves clarity.
steps.verification: Run production build and responsive smoke review -> expected: charts render from real API data and core screens work on desktop/mobile widths -> PASS; must-fail: unreadable charts, broken layout, or inaccessible primary actions.

steps.content: Implement AI expense categorization.
steps.implementation_outline: Create a controlled OpenAI integration, prompt/schema for category classification, fallback behavior, confidence handling, cost-conscious request boundaries, and user-editable final category assignment.
steps.verification: Run deterministic fixture prompts/mocks -> expected: supported transactions map to valid categories and malformed AI output is safely rejected -> PASS; must-fail: AI output directly mutates data without validation.

steps.content: Implement financial intelligence features without unnecessary ML complexity.
steps.implementation_outline: Build rule/query-based Money Leak Detector, Spending Forecast using transparent historical calculations, What Changed analysis, Budget Pulse, and Goal Reality Check; expose explanations alongside results.
steps.verification: Run fixture datasets with known outcomes -> expected: insights match expected calculations and explain their basis -> PASS; must-fail: opaque or fabricated financial claims.

steps.content: Implement Ask Your Money and AI monthly financial story.
steps.implementation_outline: Create an AI service that retrieves only relevant user-owned financial aggregates, constructs bounded prompts, validates responses, handles failures, and generates monthly summaries/recommendations without exposing sensitive cross-user data.
steps.verification: Run mocked AI integration tests and data-isolation tests -> expected: correct user context only, valid response shape, graceful provider failure -> PASS; must-fail: cross-user data exposure or unvalidated model output.

steps.content: Add Redis only for demonstrated performance/background needs.
steps.implementation_outline: Introduce Redis for targeted caching or rate limiting after measuring/identifying a concrete need; define TTL/invalidation rules and keep PostgreSQL as source of truth.
steps.verification: Run cache/rate-limit tests -> expected: correct hit/miss/invalidation behavior without stale financial truth -> PASS; must-fail: financial correctness depending solely on stale cache.

steps.content: Add automated testing and security hardening.
steps.implementation_outline: Expand unit, service, API, authentication, authorization, analytics, and AI-boundary tests; validate secrets, CORS, cookie settings, input limits, error handling, and dependency configuration.
steps.verification: Run full test suite and security checklist -> expected: tests pass and known auth/data-isolation cases are covered -> PASS; must-fail: failing critical auth or ownership tests.

steps.content: Containerize the full application and define local production-like orchestration.
steps.implementation_outline: Create Dockerfiles and Docker Compose for frontend, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and Redis as needed; configure environment variables and health checks; document startup flow.
steps.verification: Run docker compose build/up and health checks -> expected: services start and communicate successfully -> PASS; must-fail: missing service dependency or secrets baked into images.

steps.content: Prepare deployment and production configuration.
steps.implementation_outline: Choose deployment targets, configure production environment variables, database migrations, frontend/backend builds, CORS/origin settings, logging, health endpoints, and basic operational documentation.
steps.verification: Deploy a production build and perform smoke tests -> expected: login, transaction CRUD, dashboard, and AI endpoint work in production -> PASS; must-fail: exposed secrets or broken database migration.

steps.content: Polish portfolio presentation and document the system.
steps.implementation_outline: Create README architecture diagram, feature walkthrough, setup instructions, API overview, database diagram, screenshots, trade-offs, security notes, and a concise project story suitable for interviews.
steps.verification: Review README by following setup from a clean environment -> expected: another developer can understand and run the project -> PASS; must-fail: undocumented required secrets/steps or misleading architecture claims.

plans.user_plan_request: Create a full-fledged development plan for Smart Expense Tracker in the Smart-Expense-Tracker workspace, covering product scope, frontend, backend, PostgreSQL database, API design, authentication, AI features, testing, Docker, and deployment, while teaching the concepts step by step.
plans.conscience_rules: Follow the agreed stack and MVP scope; prioritize learning and maintainable architecture over unnecessary libraries; make UX/UI decisions early; do not over-engineer; verify each implementation step before marking it done; pause for human approval whenever a UX/mockup step is completed.
approved_deviations: User explicitly approved proceeding with frontend implementation after UX approval, so the React application shell/routing work will begin before backend/database implementation; API-backed features remain blocked until their backend contracts exist.
User approved switching the AI provider from OpenAI to the Gemini API; use Gemini-specific integration while preserving the AI service abstraction.
plans.scope_in: React + TypeScript + Vite frontend; Tailwind CSS; shadcn/ui; React Router; Recharts; Framer Motion where useful; native fetch initially; Python + FastAPI + Pydantic + SQLAlchemy + Alembic backend; PostgreSQL; Redis where justified; OpenAI integration; JWT + HttpOnly-cookie authentication; expenses, income, categories, budgets, savings goals, dashboard analytics, AI categorization, money-leak detection, spending forecast, what-changed analysis, goal reality check, Ask Your Money, monthly AI story, personalized recommendations; tests; Docker; deployment.
plans.scope_out: Bank/UPI API synchronization; paid subscriptions; OCR receipt scanning; investment tracking; credit-score integration; family/shared accounts; complex ML prediction systems; unnecessary state-management libraries; TanStack Query unless a later demonstrated need justifies it.
plans.why: The project is intended to be both a portfolio-grade full-stack application and a structured backend/frontend learning project. The plan deliberately starts with product and UX foundations, then establishes architecture and data contracts before implementation, and finishes with AI, quality, and deployment.
